title: Accept the DG-07 release and milestone contract subset
outcome: The authoritative release-slice contract and subordinate planning documents consistently record the explicitly approved PRODUCT-001 slice ownership and catalog-derived milestone meanings without changing catalog IDs, resolving deferred product gaps, or claiming any application flow delivered.
scope: Accept Slice 1 ownership of complete AUTH-001 through AUTH-004, WORKSPACE-001, PEOPLE-001, PEOPLE-002, the typed but still-planned PEOPLE-003 shell, workspace/member settings, and the cataloged public home/features route, state, navigation, and accessibility contracts without adding a public-page flow ID.
Accept PEOPLE-004 as one indivisible edit/archive/restore/delete mutation flow completed in Slice 2 and remove the fictional Slice 1 read-only subset.
Accept complete PEOPLE-003 in Slice 6 only after every enabled core person section exists while retaining its planned typed shell in Slice 1.

Define Foundation complete, Core alpha at Slice 4, Proposed MVP, Core feature complete, Optional platform complete, Catalog complete, AI-enabled complete, and Production ready with the documented meanings; derive feature milestone cuts from the accepted catalogs rather than a fixed flow count.

Synchronize only the subordinate planning status, roadmap, traceability assignments, and current catalog-derived counts needed to remove proposal-versus-accepted contradictions while every application flow remains planned.
Add a bounded deterministic PRODUCT-001 release-contract test that self-checks catalog extraction and enforces the accepted slice and milestone contract.
nonGoals: Implement application, API, worker, database, migration, infrastructure, or user-interface behavior, or mark any flow delivered.
Add, remove, rename, reprioritize, or otherwise change stable entries in user-flows.yaml or page-catalog.yaml; public.home and public.features remain cataloged pages with no stable user-flow ID.
Decide the missing life-event mutation flow, its priority, its complete observable contract, or its effect on a later core-completeness definition.
Decide an operations user interface, stable operations page or flow ID, permissions, states, or E2E contract.
Decide whether page.flowIds is exhaustive or primary-only, or decide inherited page-state semantics.
Decide multi-workspace, security-settings, avatar, help or what-is-new, or saved-filter product behavior.
Decide external API parity, P2 page availability or feature-gating semantics, romantic metadata behavior, or optional-source import behavior.
Change AGENTS.md, architecture decisions, the canonical schema, application code, .codex, .agents, .git, or any FND-001 or FND-002 path.
Push, deploy, merge main, or claim production readiness from feature completion.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The accepted release contract assigns complete AUTH-001 through AUTH-004, WORKSPACE-001, PEOPLE-001, and PEOPLE-002 to Slice 1, starts only the planned typed PEOPLE-003 shell there, includes workspace/member settings and both cataloged public product route contracts without a new flow ID, assigns indivisible PEOPLE-004 to Slice 2, and accepts complete PEOPLE-003 only in Slice 6 after all enabled core person sections exist.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The focused PRODUCT-001 contract test passes its catalog extraction controls and fails against the base release contract because Slice 1 claims complete PEOPLE-003 and a fictional read-only PEOPLE-004 subset while the approved WORKSPACE-001, public-page, settings, Slice 2, and Slice 6 assignments remain proposal text.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The authoritative product contract defines all eight approved milestone meanings, derives milestone cuts from the accepted flow and page catalogs, records Core alpha after Slice 4, and records that the current Proposed MVP and Core feature complete cuts coincide after Slice 7 without hard-coding the current flow inventory or implying production readiness.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The focused PRODUCT-001 contract test derives priority membership and slice maxima from the catalogs/matrix, then fails because the base documents leave the milestone definitions and Slice 7 cut conditional on DG-07 approval instead of recording the approved catalog-derived contract.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Planning README, roadmap, and traceability agree with the accepted release contract and regenerated current catalog totals, distinguish accepted PRODUCT-001 decisions from remaining proposals, retain zero delivered flows, and do not present a fixed count as milestone authority.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The focused PRODUCT-001 contract test self-checks the accepted catalogs and fails because the base planning documents still label the approved assignments and milestone definitions proposed, pending, or open.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Life-event flow/priority, operations UI, page.flowIds semantics, inherited states, multi-workspace/security/avatar/help/saved-filter behavior, external API parity, P2 availability, romantic metadata, and optional-source import behavior remain explicit follow-up gates, with no new stable IDs or branch decisions introduced by PRODUCT-001.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The focused PRODUCT-001 contract test requires an explicit bounded-decision statement and deferred-gaps ledger while comparing the stable catalog identities; it fails until the accepted subset is separated from the still-open follow-up gates.

risks: A release summary that splits an atomic catalog flow can authorize incomplete E2E evidence or falsely imply delivery.
Hard-coded milestone membership can silently drift when accepted flow priorities or page entries change.
Changing catalog IDs or priorities while accepting this bounded subset could silently decide deferred product behavior.
Planning language could falsely mark planned flows delivered or imply production readiness without operational evidence.
A broad Markdown check could pass on duplicated proposal text rather than the single authoritative accepted contract; extraction and uniqueness controls must discriminate that case.
This credential-free documentation/check ticket introduces no runtime tenancy, personal-data, concurrency, or external-service behavior.
